articles.title: Ballon d’Or ceremony returns to England in nod to ‘revolutionary’ Stanley Matthews
articles.summary: Matthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hall. When football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago.
body: A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. But obviously it’s grown over the years, and now it’s a huge event. We’re very excited.”

The switch of venue to England from its usual home in Paris is a mark of respect to the man who became the first active player to receive a knighthood in 1965, a few months before retiring at the age of 50. It also provides an opportunity to recall an astonishing career that began with his local side Stoke in 1932 and made the “Wizard of Dribble” the most famous player on the planet.
points: Matthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hall.
When football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago.

articles.title: Foster drops Navarrete twice to unify three world titles
articles.summary: O'Shaquie Foster unified the WBC, WBO and IBF super-featherweight world titles with a decisive unanimous decision win over Emanuel Navarrete at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas.
body: Navarrete was relentless, as he always is, but he could scarcely land punches cleanly on Foster, who mixed in footwork and counters to keep the Mexican at bay.
As the rounds progressed, Foster grew more confident and began standing his ground to trade. By the championship rounds, Foster's corner was asking him to end the show.
The 33-year-old native of Orange, Texas, scored two knockdowns in the 12th, but Navarrete survived.
Foster said, "It was a great performance. I finished strong, and I put him down twice in the end.

articles.title: Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s outbursts are no laughing matter for fans
articles.summary: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support. In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts.
body: To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest.

The clip was widely shared, there is every chance you saw it earlier this month. The general perception, from those of a neutral stance, was that one of football’s great characters had lost the plot. To those in the room, there was a sense that it was merely the exuberant mannerisms of a quirky manager during a tricky period. But for a large section of Swindon fans, it prompted an unamused eye roll. Here we go again. The circus tent is pitched firmly in town.

Supporting a Holloway-led club is an interesting assignment. Within weeks of taking the Swindon job two years ago on Sunday, he began constructing a hostile wall towards fans by reminding them that they could “go bowling” if they did not like his methods. Last December, he had to be restrained by his players during an altercation with a fan, while he has made a habit of telling them to “jog on” if overly vocal in their criticism.

articles.title: Inglorious end as rain cancels final MotoGP race at Phillip Island in setback for Márquez
articles.summary: Treacherous conditions put end to nearly three decades at venue. Australian race will relocate to Melbourne street circuit next year. Marc Márquez was denied the chance to stretch his world championship lead over injured Jorge Martin with the last Australian MotoGP at Phillip Island cancelled due…
body: Organisers pulled the plug despite a sell-out crowd with persistent rain and poor visibility making racing unsafe. The Moto3 and Moto2 races were also called off. “Limited visibility has resulted in the cancellation of the Australian MotoGP,” organisers said.

It was an inglorious end to nearly three decades of the sport at the waterfront circuit two hours from Melbourne, with the Australian race moving to a city-centre street circuit at Adelaide next year.

While a blow for Ducati’s Márquez, it was an escape for Aprilia’s Martin, who had been ruled out of the race with a fractured forearm sustained when he crashed during the sprint on Saturday, won by his fellow Spaniard.

He risked sliding further behind seven-time world champion Márquez with only four legs of the season to go, starting next week in Malaysia. Instead he will leave Australia just 10 points adrift. Aprilia’s Marco Bezzecchi is third in the standings, 50 points behind Márquez.

articles.title: What Man Utd need now is stability, not more changes - Pulis
articles.summary: BBC Sport columnist Tony Pulis explains why Bruno Fernandes' comments after Manchester United's defeat by Como showed how hard it must be to run the club at the moment.
body: Walking into an under-achieving football club is never easy. I know, because I spent my career taking on such challenges.
That was the task Michael Carrick took on in January when he was appointed Manchester United 's interim manager and took over a club that was drifting deeper and deeper into mediocrity.
Supporters talk about seeing a bounce when new managers take over and, from my own experiences, I do believe that to be the case.

Michael certainly experienced a fantastic period where results and performances improved. In his case, United's improvement to finish third and in the Champions League places was exceptional - and he also calmed the water behind the scenes.

articles.title: What have Man Utd changed to turn around WSL form?
articles.summary: It's a different picture at Manchester United now than it was last month - so what have they changed to turn around their WSL form?
body: It is a different picture at Manchester United now than it was last month as they gear up for the derby against Women's Super League leaders Manchester City.
Eva Olid's side were without a win and low on confidence after their opening three matches in a disappointing start to the season.
But after getting their first win on the board against Sheffield United in the Women's League Cup, United have won six successive matches in all competitions.
They now sit fifth in the table, eight points off unbeaten rivals City, who they face on Sunday (18:00 GMT) hoping to continue their positive form.

articles.title: 'This is the only Clasico' - Mourinho's Real trying to stop Barca's shot at history
articles.summary: Barcelona aim to make La Liga history against Real Madrid, with Jose Mourinho looking to end their winning run.
body: Barcelona stand on the brink of La Liga history, targeting a 10th consecutive victory to start the league season.
It will surpass the mark set in 1968-69 by Real Madrid, who will have the chance to end that remarkable run on Sunday when the sides meet at Camp Nou.

Barcelona head into El Clasico on the back of a 4-2 Champions League defeat by Paris St-Germain, giving Jose Mourinho's men the perfect opportunity to capitalise on that setback and wreck the record bid of their rivals.
Real boss Mourinho has insisted his team's most recent performances, two 4-1 victories against Sevilla and RB Leipzig, would count for little in a fixture that has such global appeal and standing.

articles.title: Brewers make postseason history with incredible merchandise sales record
articles.summary: Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here. The Milwaukee Brewers are two wins away from taking down the Tampa Bay Rays for their first World Series title, and their fans have already made history of their own.
body: Brewers make postseason history with incredible merchandise sales record appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Brewers have sold more merchandise this postseason than any team in MLB history, according to Bob Nightengale of USA Today. MLB officials shared the news with Brewers owner Mark Attanasio amid the team’s historic October run.

It is the latest sign of just how much this October has meant to Milwaukee. The Brewers are back in the Fall Classic for the first time since 1982, when they fell to the St. Louis Cardinals in seven games, and the city has fully embraced the moment.

The record did not come out of nowhere. Fans started lining up for gear long before the World Series arrived. After the Brewers swept the Los Angeles Dodgers to win the National League pennant, an MLB spokesperson told the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel that sales exploded over the next two days. “More Brewers merch was sold in those 48 hours than any other pennant winner on record,” the spokesperson said.

articles.title: Alexander Volkanovski Refused to Take Even Ibuprofen Despite Being Extremely Sick at UFC 333
articles.summary: UFC 333 turned into another memorable night for Alexander Volkanovski. The 38-year-old overcame another challenge to defend his featherweight title at Etihad Arena, finishing Movsar Evloev in the second round and handing the Russian his first career loss after 20 straight wins.
body: As expected, Volkanovski’s sharp striking and excellent takedown defense made the difference. He looked quicker from the opening bell, targeting Evloev’s legs with inside low kicks before mixing in stiff jabs and powerful overhand rights.

Volkanovski eventually hurt Evloev with a big overhand right before following up with a flurry of punches that sent the Russian crashing to the canvas. He kept attacking until referee Marc Goddard stepped in with just seconds left in the second round.

But the win became even more impressive after it emerged that Volkanovski had been battling the flu during fight week. The champion reportedly refused to take any medication, believing it could give him an unfair advantage over his opponent.

The signs were there during Friday’s early-morning weigh-ins, when Volkanovski’s voice sounded noticeably different. Many initially put it down to the weight cut, but his training partner and BJJ legend Craig Jones later revealed on social media that the Aussie had been sick.

articles.title: 'Not realistic' - Can Wolff's assessment of Antonelli's title chance be trusted?
articles.summary: Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff believes it is "not realistic" for Kimi Antonelli to win the 2026 F1 Drivers' Championship on Sunday at the United States Grand Prix, despite the Italian starting on pole position.
body: Antonelli was not expected to claim top spot in qualifying but produced a superb lap in Q3 to beat Red Bull's Max Verstappen and take his first pole since July's Belgian Grand Prix.
Should Antonelli win Sunday's race in Austin with Lewis Hamilton finishing fifth or lower and George Russell no better than ninth, he will seal the title with five rounds remaining.
Hamilton will start fifth and Russell sixth when the lights go out at the Circuit of the Americas at 8pm (build-up from 6.30pm), live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event.
However, Wolff has warned Mercedes will not have the pace to win as they did not have the pace in Friday practice's long runs.

articles.title: ‘Night and day different’ – why did Ferrari's pace evaporate again?
articles.summary: Ferrari's wait for a first Grand Prix pole position since August 2025 continued in the United States on Saturday as Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton qualified outside the top three in a session the team had appeared favourites for.
body: For the first time this season, Ferrari went into qualifying having topped all three practice sessions in Austin, on a weekend their car features the team's final significant upgrade of the season.
Leclerc finished second fastest to McLaren's Lando Norris in Q1, but only after the McLaren driver completed a second run to do so, and then returned to the head of the field in Q2.
But the Scuderia found themselves on the back foot immediately from the start of Q3 with Leclerc holding a provisional fourth and Hamilton sixth after the first runs of the decisive final phase.

Hamilton improved one place to fifth on his final run, but Leclerc stayed where he was, to leave the Ferraris behind the two Red Bull drivers and Mercedes polesitter Kimi Antonelli for the start of Sunday's 56-lap race.
